title: Associated sheaf of a K-flat complex on an affine scheme is K-flat
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring and $X=\operatorname{Spec}(A)$ [def-pc-scheme]. Let $K^\bullet$ be a cochain complex of $A$-modules that is K-flat, i.e. for every acyclic complex $F^\bullet$ of $A$-modules the total tensor complex $\operatorname{Tot}(F^\bullet\otimes_AK^\bullet)$ is acyclic. Let $\widetilde{K^\bullet}$ be the complex of $\mathcal O_X$-modules obtained by applying the associated sheaf $\widetilde{(-)}$ [lem-weil-pbc-spec-module-tilde-sections] termwise, with differentials $\widetilde{d^n}$. Then $\widetilde{K^\bullet}$ is a K-flat complex of $\mathcal O_X$-modules [def-pc-kflat-complex].

source.place: Lemma 36.3.6 (Tag 08DV, perfect-lemma-affine-K-flat), perfect.tex lines 326-342; proof via More on Algebra 064K (base change of K-flat), Cohomology 06YB (stalk criterion), Schemes 01HV

proof.text: Fix a point x of X, corresponding to a prime ideal p of A. The stalk of the associated sheaf of each term of K^\bullet is canonically K^n_p, and these identifications commute with the differentials; hence the stalk complex (\widetilde{K^\bullet})_x is the localization complex K^\bullet \otimes_A A_p, by the affine associated-sheaf stalk computation (Tag 01HV).

For every prime p, the complex K^\bullet \otimes_A A_p is K-flat over A_p (base change of a K-flat complex, Tag 06Y1): if L^\bullet is an acyclic complex of A_p-modules, it is also an acyclic complex of A-modules by restriction of scalars, and termwise L^a \otimes_{A_p} (K^b \otimes_A A_p) \cong L^a \otimes_A K^b naturally, compatibly with the differentials and signs, so \operatorname{Tot}(L^\bullet \otimes_{A_p} (K^\bullet \otimes_A A_p)) \cong \operatorname{Tot}(L^\bullet \otimes_A K^\bullet), which is acyclic by the K-flatness of K^\bullet.

Thus every stalk of \widetilde{K^\bullet} is K-flat. The reverse implication of the stalk criterion [lem-pc-kflat-stalk-criterion] then implies that \widetilde{K^\bullet} is K-flat as a complex of \mathcal O_X-modules.
